attacks_claim.attack_type: distribution-shift (temperature-regime extrapolation within a SINGLE source, where the receipt's applicability-domain score is purely structural and blind to T/weight-fraction)
attacks_claim.refutation_criterion: One-sided paired t-test (alpha=0.05, n=10 scaffold-partition seeds) that shifted-regime (T>308K) coverage is significantly LOWER than a matched-T control's coverage under the identical model/q_hat for that seed -- for either the full shifted test set or the AD-flagged-in-domain subset of it.
attacks_claim.target_statement: within_source_marginal_conformal_coverage_at_alpha_010_meets_target observed 0.9277 (target >=0.90) PASSED; worst_ad_quintile_coverage_at_alpha_010_meets_worst_case_floor observed 0.9000 PASSED -- i.e. within the tested polymer-scaffold AD interior, split-conformal coverage is claimed reliable.
attacks_claim.theoretical_basis: Tibshirani, Barber, Candes, Ramdas 2019 NeurIPS 'Conformal Prediction Under Covariate Shift'; split-conformal marginal coverage requires cal/test exchangeability. Applicability-domain methods restricted to structural (Morgan fingerprint) similarity (OECD 2007 Principle 3; Roy-Kar-Ambure 2015) do not certify exchangeability along covariates (temperature, weight fraction) outside the fingerprint space.

finding: Across 10 independent scaffold-partition seeds, shifted-regime (T>308K) coverage (mean 0.8899) is NOT statistically distinguishable from the matched-T control's coverage (mean 0.9121) under a one-sided paired t-test (p=0.1532 for the full shifted set, p=0.2081 for the AD-flagged-in-domain subset) -- the deficit seen in any single seed is within the range of ordinary finite-sample scaffold-holdout variance already present in the matched-T control (control coverage itself ranges 0.7768-1.0000 across seeds). The attack was genuinely capable of falsifying: had temperature-regime extrapolation caused a stable, seed-independent coverage collapse distinguishable from ordinary holdout noise, the paired test would have detected it.

scope_honesty.caveat: This survival does NOT establish that the AD-interior guarantee holds under all covariate shifts -- only that a T-regime extrapolation shift, at this sample size (n=424 shifted rows, ~10-49 scaffolds per arm), does not produce a coverage deficit distinguishable from ordinary scaffold-holdout sampling variance. The matched-T control itself swings from 0.777 to 1.0 across seeds, showing this benchmark is underpowered to detect anything but a large effect.
